sources.note: What Isp means and how it sets exhaust velocity (Isp × g0).

sources.name: NASA Glenn Research Center: Rocket Thrust and the rocket equation
sources.note: Background for Δv = Isp × g0 × ln(m0 / mf).

sources.name: NASA Space Nuclear Propulsion
sources.note: Nuclear thermal propulsion: roughly twice the efficiency of chemical rockets (game uses Isp 900 s).

sources.name: NASA Dawn mission (ion propulsion)
sources.note: Ion engines: very high Isp (around 3,000 s) with gentle thrust and kilowatts of electric power.

sources.name: Game values
sources.note: Engine masses, costs and the ion engine's 2.5 kW power draw are simplified game values.

engines.name: Basic chemical
engines.description: Simple, and it rarely fails. Each kilogram of fuel gives a small push.

engines.name: Advanced chemical
engines.description: Burns super-cold (cryogenic) liquid hydrogen and oxygen. Each kilogram of fuel gives more push.

engines.name: Nuclear
engines.description: A nuclear reactor makes hydrogen very hot. It uses fuel very well, but it is heavy and expensive.
engines.restriction: Launching a nuclear reactor needs an extra safety review. Expect a review event at launch.

engines.name: Electric (ion)
engines.description: Electricity pushes out tiny xenon particles very fast. It uses fuel extremely well. But the push is very gentle, and it needs 2.5 kW of power.
engines.restriction: Too weak to land. Use it only for the asteroid. The trip takes 3 times longer.
